Subject: Redwood vs. Hyperscaler - Bake-off plan & success criteria

Hi Samir - thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get the bake-off scheduled: 

Summary of ask:
- Vertex wants a side-by-side evaluation of Redwood Inference vs your current hyperscaler provider for text-generation and multi-turn chat workloads (customer-facing agent). Focus: latency, throughput, cost, and response quality/hallucination risk.

Proposed tests (baseline scope):
1) Latency: P50 / P95 / cold start for short (64 tokens) and long (1024 tokens) sequences.
2) Throughput: sustained QPS targets at 50 and 200 concurrent requests (batching enabled/disabled).
3) Cost: normalized cost per 1M tokens (including any required provisioned capacity).
4) Quality: run the 500-sample prompt set you shared; measure generation quality metrics + manual spot checks on hallucination/consistency.
5) Failure cases & graceful degradation: rate-limited scenarios and model fallback behavior.

Proposed test variants:
- Redwood-optimized (quantized float16 + batching + KV prefix cache)
- Redwood-default (no aggressive quantization)
- Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (your current config)

Success criteria (initial suggestion):
- P95 latency within 15% of hyperscaler for equivalent throughput OR 30% reduction in cost for same latency SLA.
- Hallucination/incorrect-answer rate <= baseline + 5% (manual review)
- Stable throughput at target QPS for 30-minute run with <1% request error rate.

Timeline & owners:
- Redwood provides test harness + prompt set: Aditya Rao (by 2027-02-17)
- Customer runs/observes live test and shares logs: Samir / Vertex (by 2027-02-24)
- Pricing & MAP draft: Vanessa Ortiz (first draft by 2027-02-18)

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-proposal.xlsx (high-level plan + sample prompt set).

Next step: if this scope looks right, can we lock in a two-week window starting 2/21 for the initial runs? Also confirm whether Vertex wants tests run in us-west-2 or us-east-1.

Thanks -
Laura Bennett

Thanks Laura - this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from my side: 

- Region: please run in us-west-2 for the initial run (that’s where our prod traffic is routed).
- Cold-start latency is important for us - please include a cold-start measurement for a VM/container start plus first request (P50/P95).
- Concurrency: can we also include a 50 QPS sustained test (our current average) and a 200 QPS spike test?
- Logs/access: we’ll need request/response logs (redacted) and cost breakdowns. Samir will share a secure transfer method - procurement is cc’d.

On timing, the two-week window starting 2/21 works for us as long as Redwood can provide the harness by 2/17. If you can also include a quick side-by-side of tokenization differences that impact costs, that would be helpful.

Appreciate the details - looking forward to the plan.

 -Samir

Got it - owners and dates look good. I attached the initial test plan and harness artifacts to speed things up: 20270210-vertex-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx and redwood-test-harness.tar.gz (small runner + README).

Marissa's test plan (high level):
1) Prep (by 2/17): Aditya to deliver docker runner, tokenization notes, and the 500-sample prompt set. I will QA the prompt set and sync timing with Samir.
2) Baseline runs (2/21-2/23): small runs to validate config and permissions.
3) Full runs (2/24-2/25):
   - Latency: P50/P95 for 64 & 1024 token sequences (cold-start and warmed)
   - Throughput: 50 QPS sustained (30 minutes) and 200 QPS spike (10 minutes)
   - Cost run: capture token counts, compute cost per 1M tokens for each variant
   - Quality: run automated scoring + 30-manual spot checks for hallucination/accuracy
4) Post-run analysis (by 2/28): consolidate logs, cost comparison, and recommended config (quantization/batching settings).

Success criteria (finalized before runs):
- P95 within 15% of hyperscaler for equivalent throughput OR >=30% cost savings at same latency SLO.
- Error rate <1% during sustained runs.
- Quality loss <=5% relative to hyperscaler on automated scoring + manual check tolerances.

I'll share the Drive folder with Samir once Aditya uploads the harness. If procurement needs anything else for secure transfers, let me know - I’ll loop in Solutions Eng.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
